title: Derived g induces the graded quotient after the image lift
statement:
Let $X$ be a type-zero bigraded exact couple in an abelian category [def-sp-exact-couple] with $D^{i,j}=0$ whenever $j<a$. Fix $p\geq0$ and any integer $q$, and put $R=\max(p+3,q-a+2)$, $r=R-2$, $u=p-r$, $v=q+r$. Let $\iota_n:D_n\to D$ be the recursively composed canonical derived-D inclusions with $\iota_0=1$. Let $F$ be a decreasing filtration of $D^{0,p+q}$ [def-sp-filtration] whose steps at every nonnegative index are the incoming alpha images [def-sp-convergence]. Fix invertible $\lambda:D^{0,p+q}\to D^{u,v}$ equal to the canonically transported $(-u)$-fold alpha iterate, and an invertible lift $\ell:F^p\to D_r^{u,v}$ with $\iota_r\circ\ell=\lambda\circ(F^p\hookrightarrow D^{0,p+q})$. Then there exists an isomorphism $\psi:\operatorname{gr}^pF\to E_R^{p,q}$ for which the cokernel projection followed by $\psi$ is $\ell$ followed by the derived-couple map $g_r$ and the canonical equality transport to $E_R^{p,q}$.

Exact Lean interface:
```lean
theorem finitePage_graded_quotient
    {B : Type u₂} [Category.{v₂} B] [Abelian B]
    (X : BigradedExactCouple B 0) (a : ℤ)
    (hDzero : ∀ p q : ℤ, q < a → IsZero (X.D p q))
    (inc : ∀ (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), (X.pageCouple r).D p q ⟶ X.D p q)
    (hinc0 : ∀ p q : ℤ, inc 0 p q = 𝟙 _)
    (hinc : ∀ (r : ℕ) (p q : ℤ), inc (r + 1) p q =
      (X.pageCouple r).derivedDInclusion p q ≫ inc r p q)
    (p q : ℤ) (hp : 0 ≤ p)
    (F : DecreasingFiltration (X.D 0 (p + q)))
    (hF : ∀ i : ℤ, 0 ≤ i → F.step i =
      imageSubobject (X.incomingAlphaIter i.toNat 0 (p + q)))
    (lambda : X.D 0 (p + q) ⟶
      X.D (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2) (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2))
    (hlambda : lambda = X.alphaIter
      (-(p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2)).toNat 0 (p + q) ≫
        eqToHom (by congr 1 <;> omega))
    [IsIso lambda]
    (lift : (F.step p : B) ⟶
        (X.pageCouple ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2)).D
          (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2)
          (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2))
    (hlift : IsIso lift)
    (hliftinc : lift ≫ inc ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2)
      (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2)
      (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2) = (F.step p).arrow ≫ lambda) :
    ∃ (psi : F.gradedPiece p ≅ X.page (max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat p q),
      cokernel.π (Subobject.ofLE (F.step (p + 1)) (F.step p)
          (F.antitone_step (by omega))) ≫ psi.hom = lift ≫
        (X.pageCouple ((max (p + 3) (q - a + 2)).toNat - 2)).g
          (p - max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) + 2)
          (q + max (p + 3) (q - a + 2) - 2) ≫
        eqToHom (by unfold BigradedExactCouple.page; congr 1 <;> omega)
```

proof.text: Use the proved private prescribed_inclusion_images and incoming_split_heq helpers of FinitePageImageLift through a proof-only import all. These identify the prescribed inc with the canonical image inclusion family from pageCouple_image and split the incoming (r+1)-fold iterate at index zero. Its image is F.step(p+1).arrow followed by lambda. The lift equation and monicity of inc and lambda identify this derived-alpha image inside derived D with the next-step inclusion in F.step(p). Derived-couple exactness identifies it with the kernel of g.

The target of the derived f map after g is derived D(p+2,q-1). It embeds by inc into the incoming r-fold image with source D(p+R,q-R+1). This source is zero since R>=q-a+2. Thus f has zero target, and derived-couple exactness makes g epi. After precomposition with lift and postcomposition with the canonical index transport it is still epi and has the next-step inclusion as kernel. Reuse the proved pageD_zero helper of HalfPlaneWeakConvergence as a generic tool for this vanishing; no half-plane convergence hypothesis or conclusion is used.

In an abelian category an epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel. Consequently the graded cokernel and page R are isomorphic by the unique map specified by their projection equation. Both p=0 and q<a satisfy the same image computation and inequality; no excluded bidegree or extra support assumption is needed. Reuse its proved quotient_comparison helper as a generic abelian-category tool.
